title: [Cloud Shell] API Error: "Requested entity was not found" when using Lab Accounts in

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides complete reproduction steps and environment details (Cloud Shell Lab account with compute-default-credentials) for an unhandled API 404 error on the default cloudshell-gca project.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The issue is a localized error handling fix in server.ts to catch 404 (Requested entity was not found) errors alongside 403 errors when using the default cloudshell-gca project, and surface a clear user-facing guidance error.

summary.problem: When running Gemini CLI in Cloud Shell using a Google Cloud Lab account, the default project 'cloudshell-gca' returns an API error 'Requested entity was not found' (404), which is unhandled and displayed directly to the user instead of displaying a helpful error message.
summary.root_cause: The loadCodeAssist method in server.ts only catches 403 Permission Denied errors when cloudaicompanionProject is 'cloudshell-gca'. It does not catch 404 Not Found errors, causing 404 responses from lab accounts to fall through to an unhandled API error.
summary.context: Cloud Shell environments default GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT to 'cloudshell-gca'. In Lab Accounts or environments where this project entity is missing/not found, the API responds with a 404 'Requested entity was not found' error rather than 403.

steps: Add a helper function or update error checks in packages/core/src/code_assist/server.ts to identify 404 (Not Found) errors in API responses.
Update the error handling in loadCodeAssist to check for both 403 (Permission Denied) and 404 (Not Found) errors when req.cloudaicompanionProject is 'cloudshell-gca'.

Throw the friendly error message advising the user to set their own Google Cloud project using 'gcloud config set project [PROJECT_ID]' or setting 'GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT' when a 404 error is encountered on 'cloudshell-gca'.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When loadCodeAssist encounters a 404 Not Found error on the 'cloudshell-gca' project, it throws the friendly error message explaining that default Cloud Shell Gemini project access was denied or not found and provides instructions on setting a project.
verification_steps: Add a unit test in packages/core/src/code_assist/server.test.ts that mocks a 404 response for loadCodeAssist with cloudaicompanionProject set to 'cloudshell-gca'.
Assert that calling loadCodeAssist rejects with an error matching /Access to the default Cloud Shell Gemini project/.
